title: decouple-lint-runtime-and-shared-dep-curator-introduce-presubmit-prioritizer
author: Amira Kline
description:
Context: Our monolithic presubmit lint runner has become a bottleneck for rapid iteration — changes to TypeScript projects block unrelated Go/Scala/Docs changes and large dependency churn PRs cause repeated flakiness. This PR decouples language/runtime lint execution into lightweight runtime-specific runners, introduces a small dependency-curator helper that annotates dependency update PRs with a stability score, and adds a presubmit prioritizer to fast-path hotpath checks for low-latency feedback. Motivation: reduce presubmit turnaround for high-velocity teams, improve signal-to-noise for dep-updates, and make staged rollouts of lint rule upgrades safer.

Changes (high level): - Split the single .github/presubmit job into per-runtime lint runners (node-lint, go-lint, python-lint, docs-lint) with a shared minimal launcher. - Add tools/dep-curator: a small Go binary that computes a heuristic stability score for a dependency (based on release cadence, semver, vulnerability tags from DB) and writes status/context to dependency PRs. - Add scripts/presubmit-prioritizer.py: inspects changed files in a PR and triggers only the subset of runtimes that touch the changed paths; optionally triggers a full lint when a config/infra file changes. - Introduce a lightweight presubmit cache key based on changed directories to fast-skip irrelevant runners. - Update docs and contributor guide with migration notes and rollback plan. Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1892) [x] Unit tests for prioritizer script [x] Integration smoke on ephemeral runners [x] Canary rollout to a 10% subset of active repos using repo flag [x] CI green on second run Known tradeoffs/risks: - Slightly more YAML in workflows; mitigated with templateization. - Dep-curator uses a best-effort heuristic and should not be relied on as a blocker; it only annotates and suggests labels. Migration steps: - Roll out workflow changes in canary mode for 2 days. - Observe presubmit latency and queue depth (console dashboards updated). - If regressions, revert to previous workflow via rollback branch hook. Rollout & follow-ups: - Add a nightly job that recalculates dep-curator scores for open dependency PRs. - Add opt-in strict gating for specific teams where dep stability matters more. Why this is different from similar past PRs: instead of trimming CI matrix or batching tests, this PR focuses on separation of runtime execution and active prioritization per-PR to reduce end-to-end feedback latency while providing structured metadata (stability score) for dependency automation.

review_comments: Marco Chen (reviewer): Can we keep the monolith as a fallback path? If a templated job fails, we should still be able to run the old combined job. Author: added canary flag and a fallback job that can be enabled via repo settings.

Lena Ortega (reviewer): dep-curator sounds useful, but please ensure it never blocks merges. Suggestion: annotate only and add an opt-in action to auto-merge when score>0.8. Author: implemented annotation-only behavior and added an opt-in label automation in contrib/.
Priya Nair (approver): Verified that the prioritizer reduces Node-only presubmit runs on a sample of 150 PRs; latency improved by ~40%. Approving pending minor nit on caching script (fixed).
CI automation: lint and test passed after second attempt; first run hit flaky network test, rerun cleared it.
release_notes: - Decouple presubmit lint into runtime-specific jobs to reduce feedback latency. - Add tools/dep-curator to annotate dependency PRs with a stability score (non-blocking). - Introduce presubmit prioritizer to only run relevant runtimes per-PR. Impact: faster presubmit for most PRs; no breaking changes to developer workflow.
